brief: Rank competing goals using the learner’s stated deadlines and consequences.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Choose an order"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Elige un orden"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Escolha uma ordem"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Rank competing goals using the learner’s stated deadlines and consequences.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: Order goals using their deadlines and stated consequences.
instruction.misconception: Automatically prioritize the cheapest or most attractive goal.
instruction.numeracy_support: The worked examples introduce the required operation; every assessed task retains its own amounts and assumptions.

evidence.reasoning: A 30-dollar repair prevents tomorrow’s work disruption; a decoration can wait. The deadline and consequence justify doing the repair first.
The stated health consequence and deadline justify priority.

Consequences matter beyond the sticker price.
A marketing deadline does not erase an essential obligation.
Missing constraints prevent a justified ranking.
